title: The paper bridge

intro.bo: {nome}, today you build something with your hands: a paper bridge. First you think, then you test, then you improve it.
intro.pilu: {nome}, can a sheet of paper become a bridge? Let's think, then really test it.
intro.tango: A paper bridge, {nome}! I'd knock it down right away, but you think and guess first. Then we test!

outro.bo: You thought, tested and changed things, {nome}. There are many ways to build a bridge: yours is one.
outro.pilu: Well done, {nome}. There is never just one bridge: you can build more and compare them.
outro.tango: Your bridge is done, {nome}! Invent another tomorrow? I'll hold the books.

offscreen: You need a sheet of paper (later two), two books, some coins and a bit of tape. Build the bridge for real and add the coins one at a time. Ask 'what do you think will happen?' and 'what would you change?' without saying whether it is right: the test decides, and every bridge that holds is a good solution.

levels.goal: Build a paper bridge between two books.
levels.criterion: Does the bridge hold a coin?

phases.label: How will you build your bridge?
phases.say: Think about how to make the sheet stay between the two books. You can fold it, roll it, however you like. Then tell me your idea.

phases.label: Will it hold the coin?
phases.say: Before you test it, guess: will the coin stay on the bridge? Tell me why you think so.

phases.label: Really test it
phases.say: Put the coin on the bridge with your own hands. Then tell me how it went.

phases.label: What would you change?
phases.say: Look at your bridge. What would you change to make it stronger, or to build it another way? If you like, try it.

levels.goal: Build a longer paper bridge, with the books further apart.
levels.criterion: Does the bridge hold five coins?

phases.label: How will you make it stronger?
phases.say: Now the books are further apart. How will you use the sheets? You can stack one on the other, or fold them like an accordion. Tell me your idea.

phases.label: How many coins will it hold?
phases.say: Before you test it, guess: how many coins will the bridge hold? Why do you think so?

phases.label: Really test it
phases.say: Add the coins one at a time, with your own hands. Then tell me how it went.

phases.label: What did you change?
phases.say: What did you change from your first idea? Are there other ways to build it? Try one.
